result:
Report written to `/tmp/diffreview/DIFFERENTIAL_REVIEW_REPORT.md` (kept out of the repo — read-only review). Verified with `cargo check --all-features` (clean) and `cargo test --lib --all-features network::connection_pool` (8 pass; `many_connections` fails identically on `main` — it needs a live cluster).

The headline issue is F1: `current_keyspace` is stored optimistically and never rolled back (`session.rs:2008`, `worker.rs:351`, `connection_pool.rs:1287`). Pre-PR, a failed `use_keyspace("does_not_exist")` was merely a correctness bug — the connection got published anyway. Post-PR, every new connection is discarded, so pools never fill, the refiller churns full handshakes against every node forever at `max_fill_backoff`, and as existing connections die the pools drain to `Broken` and the nodes drop out of load balancing. The fix needs the permanent-vs-transient split that `use_keyspace_result` already makes at `cluster/worker.rs:783`.

Secondary: the metrics-balancing commit fixes three of four discard sites — `connection_pool.rs:994` (shard-mismatch drop) still leaks, as does refiller teardown, which the new test at `:2011` actually encodes.
